data.turoyo: Ḥa yawmo may yawmoṯe d aloho hawi ʕaǧəz, komər qayəm, nafəq l qarʕa di goro, d šoqəl hawa, howe mətsayyər, <...>
data.translation: Eines Tags von den Tagen Gottes wurde er müde und stieg auf das Dach, um Luft zu schöpfen und sich ein wenig zu ergehen. <...>

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: masculine subject with howe contrasts with the existing feminine hawyono context.

summary: Both occurrences predicate strolling with a form of hwy and mətsayyər; no direct object or new valency is attested.
105/97 feminine hawyono and 108/23 masculine howe occur with the same printed mətsayyər form. Preserve source spelling rather than inferring gender inflection or a new box.
The purpose phrase 'take air' gives the recreational context; it does not establish an additional sense of tsyr or a light-verb meaning.
The existing t-bearing tsyr entry and its stem I label are retained. These two forms alone do not settle its relationship to separately filed syr or establish another finite paradigm.
Does mətsayyər function as an invariant borrowed predicate or as a productive Part act. with inflection?
What motivates separate tsyr versus syr entries in the editors' analysis? These two citations do not justify merging or relabelling them.
